data.content_ref: inline:The proposed relation (integration) is semantically incoherent on its own terms. SRC_001 defines the checklist as a 'low-pass filter' that 'eliminates high-frequency omission errors,' yet then frames the refutation around 'misinterpretation of high-frequency signals' that 'the filter removes.' A low-pass filter by definition attenuates high-frequency components, so if the 'expert intuition' signal is high-frequency, the filter's removal of it is the mechanism working as designed — not a failure of the integration. The refutation condition misidentifies the filter's own operation as a defect, rendering the relation self-contradictory rather than a substantive integration. A genuine integration would refute if the filter eliminated a LOW-frequency structural signal that the checklist needs for floor-raising, not the high-frequency signal it is explicitly designed to discard.
